mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(3)</annotation></semantics></math>, the height of the graph. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P'(3)</annotation></semantics></math> is the slope of the tangent line.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P'(3)</annotation></semantics></math> is less than the average rate, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>

options: Each derivative with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> contains <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is a function of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, so the chain rule multiplies by its derivative

It is the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: The edge <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> of a cube grows at 0.1 cm per second. How fast is its volume <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V = s^3</annotation></semantics></math> growing when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = 4</annotation></semantics></math> cm? Include units.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3s^2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = 4</annotation></semantics></math>; multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{ds}{dt} = 0.1</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the volume times the rate. Differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^3</annotation></semantics></math> first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3s^2\frac{ds}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Water fills a cylindrical tank of radius 3 meters, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V = 9\pi h</annotation></semantics></math>. The water level rises at 0.2 meters per minute. How fast is the volume increasing? Include units.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dV}{dh}</annotation></semantics></math>; multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dh}{dt} = 0.2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The volume of a cylinder uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2 = 9</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V = \pi r^2 h = 9\pi h</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Here <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> are functions of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + y^2 = 100</annotation></semantics></math>. Which equation follows?

The area of a circular stain grows at a constant rate, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dA}{dt} = 5</annotation></semantics></math> cm² per second. As the stain gets larger, what happens to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>?

A sphere's radius grows at 0.5 cm per second. How fast is its surface area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S = 4\pi r^2</annotation></semantics></math> growing when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> cm? Include units.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\pi r</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math>; multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt} = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

The power rule on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2r</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi \cdot 2r = 8\pi r</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The foot of the 10-foot ladder slides away from the wall at 2 feet per second. How fast is the top moving when the foot is 6 feet from the wall? Include units.

mistakes.why: The top moves down, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> is negative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The top and foot do not move at equal speeds; their rates are linked by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: How fast is the top of the ladder moving when the foot is 8 feet from the wall? Include units.

mistakes.why: Check which length goes where: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{8}{6} \cdot 2</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 8</annotation></semantics></math> on top.
The top is sliding down, so its rate is negative.

items.q: A student writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6^2 + y^2 = 100</annotation></semantics></math> first and then differentiates. Why does that lose the answer?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6^2</annotation></semantics></math> is a constant, so the term with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 2</annotation></semantics></math> disappears

The equation <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6^2 + y^2 = 100</annotation></semantics></math> is false at this instant

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> be the angle between the ladder and the floor, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \frac{x}{10}</annotation></semantics></math>. How fast is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> changing when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 6</annotation></semantics></math>? Include units.

mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>; the angle is shrinking as the ladder slides, so the rate is negative.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is the opposite side over the hypotenuse, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>y</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y}{10} = 0.8</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x}{10} = 0.6</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At the same instant (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h = 2</annotation></semantics></math>), how fast is the radius of the water's surface growing? Include units.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dh}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \frac{h}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{dh}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is half of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, so its rate is half of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dh}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>, not double.

Differentiate both sides with respect to time

mistakes.why: That is the plane's ground speed. The distance to the station grows more slowly, by the factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>z</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x}{z}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Sand falls onto a conical pile whose height always equals its radius. Which equation should be differentiated to find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dh}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dV}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>?

A spherical snowball melts so that its volume decreases at 10 cubic centimeters per minute. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> when the radius is 5 cm, with units (the sign matters).

mistakes.why: The volume is decreasing, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dV}{dt} = -10</annotation></semantics></math> and the radius shrinks: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt} < 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

That divides by the volume formula <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3</annotation></semantics></math>. Use its derivative, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi r^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A point moves along the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^2</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?
